experiment_description: Central concept: inelastic x-ray scattering (IXS) is used as a direct density-response probe from which the quantum Fisher information density f_Q, Bures metric g_q, and longitudinal quantum weight K(q) of insulating solids can be obtained, enabling comparison of quantum-information delocalization in covalently bonded diamond and ionically bonded LiF. The experiment uses room-temperature IXS at Sector 9-ID of the Advanced Photon Source. A liquid-nitrogen-cooled Si(111) primary monochromator and Si(333) secondary channel-cut prepare the incident beam. For diamond, spectra are collected at incident photon energy 8981.8 eV using a Ge(733) backscattering analyzer with 0.3 eV energy resolution and momentum transfer q parallel to crystallographic direction (1,-1,0). For LiF, spectra are collected at incident photon energy 6482.5 eV using a Ge(531) analyzer with 140 meV energy resolution and q parallel to (1,0,0). The nominal momentum resolution is about 0.15 Å^-1. Energy-loss scans are obtained by scanning the incident energy over electronic excitations up to 100 eV; the plotted momentum-transfer sequence spans approximately q = 0.32 to 4.55 Å^-1. The quasi-elastic contribution below about 3 eV is removed, and the remaining spectra are treated as the dynamic structure factor/density response for electronic excitations above the band gaps. The spatial sampling area, beam footprint, number of probed sample positions, and sample mosaic/defect mapping are not specified in the text; the geometric scope explicitly reported is the reciprocal-space direction and momentum-resolution window. The spectra are converted to χ''(q,ω) in physical units by enforcing the f-sum rule after extrapolating intensity above the 100 eV cutoff as I(q,ℏω>Ω)=c(q)Ω^3/(ℏω)^3, where Ω=100 eV and c(q) is the average spectral intensity from 94 to 100 eV at fixed q. The partial f-sum normalization uses eight active electrons per primitive diamond unit cell with primitive lattice constant 2.52 Å and ten active electrons per LiF primitive unit cell with primitive lattice constant 2.84 Å. The analysis computes g_q=-(ℏ/π)∫_0^∞dω tanh(βω/2)χ''(q,ω) and f_Q=4g_q at room temperature, with β the inverse thermal energy; for the high-energy electronic spectrum the Bose factor is effectively unity.

lif_small_q_qfi_power_law_exponent.description: The approximate exponent of the small-momentum power-law decrease of the quantum Fisher information density in LiF as a function of q.

diamond_qfi_relative_to_lif_over_measure.description: The material ordering of the quantum Fisher information density when comparing diamond and LiF over the common measured momentum-transfer range.

experiment_description: Central concept: the same IXS-derived density response can be Kramers-Kronig transformed to obtain the static electronic longitudinal dielectric response needed to test quantum-geometric electrostatic bounds. The experiment uses the room-temperature IXS spectra of diamond and LiF described for the quantum-Fisher-information measurement, with elastic scattering removed and spectra scaled by the f-sum rule using the finite 100 eV electronic window and the ω^-3 high-energy extrapolation. The real part χ'(q,ω) is computed from χ''(q,ω) using the Kramers-Kronig relation χ'(q,ω)=(2/π)P∫_0^∞ dω' [ω'χ''(q,ω')/(ω'^2-ω^2)], where P denotes the principal value. The static electronic dielectric function is then obtained from ε(q,ω)^-1 = 1 + V(q)χ(q,ω), with V(q)=4πe^2/q^2, evaluated at a small nonzero energy inside the electronic gap; the figure caption specifies extraction below the gap at 4.5 eV. Momentum transfers are along (1,-1,0) for diamond and (1,0,0) for LiF, with momentum resolution about 0.15 Å^-1. The high-q spatial-frequency regime is analyzed by fitting the extracted ε(q) for q approximately greater than 2.5 Å^-1 to the short-wavelength screening form ε(q)=1+exp(-αq), where q is in Å^-1 and α is the fitted real-space decay length in Å associated with atomic-scale electronic polarization. The beam footprint, number of real-space locations, and independent sample count are not specified; homogeneity is assessed only through the reciprocal-space q-dependent dielectric response extracted from the spectra.

diamond_dielectric_high_q_decay_length_A.description: The fitted decay length α of the high-momentum electronic dielectric response of diamond using ε(q)=1+exp(-αq).

lif_dielectric_high_q_decay_length_A.description: The fitted decay length α of the high-momentum electronic dielectric response of LiF using ε(q)=1+exp(-αq).

experiment_description: Central concept: the IXS-derived Bures metric is converted into the dimensionless longitudinal quantum weight aK(q), a reciprocal-space measure of electronic localization and quantum-information sharing in insulating bonds, to compare a covalent insulator, diamond, against an ionic insulator, LiF. The analysis uses the same room-temperature IXS density-response spectra, elastic-line removal, f-sum normalization, ω^-3 extrapolation above 100 eV, and q directions as in the QFI measurement: diamond at 8981.8 eV with Ge(733) analyzer, 0.3 eV energy resolution, q parallel to (1,-1,0); LiF at 6482.5 eV with Ge(531) analyzer, 140 meV energy resolution, q parallel to (1,0,0); momentum resolution about 0.15 Å^-1. The measured q range used for the quantum-weight plot is the finite-q electronic-response range shown in the paper, approximately q≈1.5–4.6 Å^-1 for diamond and q≈1.3–3.8 Å^-1 for LiF. The quantity compared is aK(q)=-(πa/2q^2)f_Q, equivalently proportional to a g_q/q^2, where a is the primitive lattice constant, q is the magnitude of the momentum transfer, f_Q is the quantum Fisher information density, and g_q is the Bures metric obtained from χ''(q,ω). The interpretation is that aK(q) below or above unity in the small-q limit distinguishes charge fluctuations largely confined within one primitive unit cell from fluctuations extending over multiple primitive unit cells. The real-space beam footprint, scan area, number of sample locations, and defect/edge exclusion criteria are not specified; the reported homogeneity context is the reproducibility of the q-dependent reciprocal-space trend after applying the stated spectral normalization and elastic removal.

diamond_small_q_dimensionless_quantum_we.description: The inferred small-momentum category of the dimensionless quantum weight aK(q) for diamond relative to unity.

lif_small_q_dimensionless_quantum_weight.description: The inferred small-momentum category of the dimensionless quantum weight aK(q) for LiF relative to unity.

small_q_dimensionless_quantum_weight_mat.description: The inferred material ordering of the small-momentum dimensionless quantum weight aK(q).

experiment_description: Central concept: the experimentally extracted dimensionless quantum weight aK(q) is tested against wavevector-dependent electrostatic bounds that constrain the possible quantum geometry of density fluctuations in an insulator. The test uses room-temperature IXS spectra of diamond and LiF scaled by the f-sum rule, extrapolated above Ω=100 eV as ω^-3, converted to χ''(q,ω), integrated to obtain f_Q and g_q, and combined with ε(q) extracted from the Kramers-Kronig procedure. Diamond is measured with q parallel to (1,-1,0), incident energy 8981.8 eV, Ge(733) analyzer, and 0.3 eV energy resolution; LiF is measured with q parallel to (1,0,0), incident energy 6482.5 eV, Ge(531) analyzer, and 140 meV energy resolution; both use momentum resolution about 0.15 Å^-1 and room-temperature electronic energy-loss scans up to 100 eV. The bounds evaluated are (1-ε(q)^-1)E_g ≤ 4e^2K(q) ≤ sqrt(1-ε(q)^-1)ℏω_p, with the dimensionless plotted quantity multiplied by the primitive lattice constant a. Here ε(q) is the electronic static longitudinal dielectric function extracted from IXS, E_g is the smallest electronic excitation gap used for the material, ω_p=sqrt(4πne^2/m) is the plasma frequency defined using the effective electron density n from the partial f-sum rule, e is the elementary charge, m is the bare electron mass, and K(q) is the longitudinal quantum weight derived from the Bures metric. The q-dependent comparison is made over the same finite momentum ranges as the aK(q) extraction. The spatial/geometric scope is reciprocal-space only; beam footprint, real-space scan area, and number of independently measured sample positions are not specified.

diamond_quantum_weight_within_q_dependen.description: Whether the measured finite-q dimensionless quantum weight values for diamond satisfy the experimentally evaluated q-dependent electrostatic bounds.

lif_quantum_weight_within_q_dependent_el.description: Whether the measured finite-q dimensionless quantum weight values for LiF satisfy the experimentally evaluated q-dependent electrostatic bounds.

diamond_zero_q_bound_position_category.description: The qualitative position approached by the inferred small-q diamond quantum weight within the zero-wavevector electrostatic bound interval.

lif_zero_q_bound_position_category.description: The qualitative position approached by the inferred small-q LiF quantum weight within the zero-wavevector electrostatic bound interval.
